title: Puckworks parameter record
description: One record of the Puckworks parameter registry (docs/PLAN.md §7.3, module R). Records live in data/params/*.yaml, in a top-level `parameters` list next to `schema: puckworks.parameters/1`. Cross-field rules (unit vocabulary, value and prior inside the range, DOI syntax, research-note references) are checked by `puckworks-tools validate-registry`. Conventions are documented in python/README.md.

id.description: Unique dotted identifier, lower case: segments of letters, digits and underscores, e.g. hydraulics.permeability.in_shot. Ids form a tree: no id may be a prefix (at a dot) of another.

symbol.description: Symbol used in the research notes or model specs, e.g. κ_eff.

description.description: What the parameter is, in one or two sentences.

units.description: A unit string defined in data/schema/units.yaml; "1" for dimensionless.

value.description: Point value as stated by the source (typical, central or best estimate). Omit when the source gives only a range.

conditions.description: Conditions under which the value holds (temperature, method, equipment, grind).

tag.description: measured: measured directly in the cited source; derived: calculated from measured or tabulated inputs without fitting (by the source or in a research note); estimated: judgement, extrapolation, analogy or class assignment; fitted: obtained by fitting a model to data.

evidence_grade.description: Evidence key of the research notes: A peer-reviewed primary measurement; B peer-reviewed model, fit or indirect inference; C thesis, book or review; D community or grey literature.

research_note_ref.description: Section of a research note in docs/research, as "NN §X.Y", "NN Implications", "NN Implications A" or "NN Open questions" (NN = note number), or a list of such references.

used_by.description: Modules of docs/PLAN.md §7.3 that read the parameter.

licence_note.description: Licence or terms that apply to reusing the value (docs/PLAN.md §11).

comment.description: Caveats, other reported values, and markers such as [unverified] or [derived] copied from the research notes.

status.description: draft until the maintainer has reviewed the record.

relation.description: How the parameter follows from, or is linked to, other parameters: `formula` states the relation (with the numbers a note used, if any); `derived_from` lists the registry ids it can be computed from. Required when tag is derived; every id must exist in the registry.

range.description: Admissible bounds (inclusive): physical limits such as 0–1 for a fraction or ≥ 0 for a positive quantity, or the scope the plan supports (docs/PLAN.md §4, e.g. doses of 7–25 g). Leave a side out when it is unbounded. Priors and values must lie inside.

doi.description: Bare DOI, e.g. 10.3390/foods12152871 (no 'doi:' or URL prefix).

locator.description: Where in the source: table, figure, section or equation.

prior.description: Prior distribution. A stated range a–b becomes uniform(a, b), or lognormal with lower = a, upper = b, coverage = 0.95 when a > 0 and b/a > 10; 'x ± s' becomes normal(x, s); a range with a typical value becomes triangular. A prior should include every value the record cites unless the comment says why not. A parameter that must be fitted per grinder or setup, with evidence from only one or two, gets a lognormal whose 95% interval extends the evidence by a factor √2 on each side (a stated judgement).

prior_lognormal.description: Either median and geometric standard deviation, or a central interval [lower, upper] holding `coverage` of the probability.
